- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows when sentiment is positive (especially >0.3) — model tends to overshoot upward momentum.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or near-zero — model fails to capture downward pressure or volatility.
- Forecast tends to lag true price movements by 1–3 days; correct by adding 0.5–1.0 to forecast if sentiment is positive and price is rising.
- After sharp spikes (e.g., >1.5% from prior day), model overcorrects and forecasts a drop — adjust downward by 0.5–1.0 if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- Mean reversion bias: model often overpredicts mid-term trends; reduce forecast by 0.3–0.8 if sentiment is weak or sentiment history shows recent volatility.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates final price — add 0.5–1.5 to final forecast if sentiment is positive and price has been trending up.
- If sentiment is high and price is rising, model often fails to capture the full momentum — increase forecast by 0.3–0.7 for the next 3–5 days.
